title: Vikings Retains Top Spot in NAIA Women’s Wrestling Rankings
body: KANSAS CITY, MO.- Grand View (Iowa) holds the No. 1 position in the latest NAIA Women's Wrestling Coaches' Top 20, collecting 189 points to remain atop the rankings. The Vikings also have a new individual No. 1, as Cailin Campbell claimed the top spot at 117 pounds.

title: Teague Moore Named National Wrestling Hall of Fame Executive Director
body: STILLWATER, Okla. – The National Wrestling Hall of Fame announced on Wednesday that it has named Teague Moore as its new executive director. Moore's appointment was approved by the Hall of Fame's Board of Governors. He succeeds Lee Roy Smith, who has served as executive director since 2004.

title: Virginia Tech’s win over Lehigh highlighted solid week of Division I men’s dual competition
body: Manheim, Pennsylvania – With no ranked teams falling to unranked opponents last week, there was minimal movement in the latest NWCA Division I Men's Wrestling Coaches Poll presented by Theraworx, released on Tuesday. Nineteen of the 25 ranked teams held their spots, and Penn State remained No. 1 with 16 first-place votes.

title: McPherson College Athletics Adds Women’s Wrestling as 22nd Varsity Sport
body: Director of Athletics Josh Daume announced today that McPherson College will expand to 22 varsity sports with the addition of a Women's Wrestling program. The program will begin competition in the 2027-2028 academic year.

title: Ohio University Wrestling Expands Opportunities with New NCWA Program
body: ATHENS, OH – November 4, 2026 – A passion for wrestling and a determination to continue competing have inspired Ohio University junior Josh Alexander to establish a new collegiate wrestling program that will compete in the National Collegiate Wrestling Association (NCWA) during the 2026–27 season.

title: NAIA Approves Fifth Year of Eligibility
body: KANSAS CITY, Mo. – The National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics (NAIA) membership has approved a fifth year of eligibility, replacing the current four-year limit.

title: Little movement in first Division I Men’s Wrestling Coaches Poll of regular season
body: Manheim, Pennsylvania – With just seven duals involving ranked teams during the opening week of the season, there was minimal movement in the first regular-season NWCA Division I Men's Wrestling Coaches Poll presented by Theraworx, released on Wednesday. Sixteen of the 25 teams held their spots, and there were no upsets of ranked teams to shake things up.

title: National Wrestling Hall of Fame Announces Class of 2027
body: The National Wrestling Hall of Fame on Thursday announced that its Class of 2027 is Distinguished Members Afsoon Roshanzamir Johnston, Iris Smith, Thad Turner and Joe Warren; Meritorious Official honoree Michael Chase; Order of Merit recipient Dan Russell; Medal of Courage recipient Ben Kjar; and Outstanding American honoree Retired United States Navy Admiral Richard W. Mies.

title: NCWA Approves Five-Year Eligibility Rule
body: DALLAS, TX – November 1, 2026 – The National Collegiate Wrestling Association (NCWA) is pleased to announce that its Board of Directors has unanimously approved a significant change to the Association's athletic eligibility requirements, extending the maximum period of collegiate wrestling eligibility from four years to five years.

title: Genevieve Duxbury Named Head Women's Wrestling Coach
body: BEREA, Ohio – Baldwin Wallace University Athletics has announced that Genevieve Duxbury has been named the second head coach in the history of the women's wrestling program.

title: Defending Champion Wartburg Opens 2026-27 Atop NWCA Division III Men’s Preseason Coaches Poll
body: Manheim, PA – The National Wrestling Coaches Association (NWCA) has released the Preseason Division III Men's Coaches Poll, and the team that ended last season on top is starting this one there too. Wartburg, which won the 2026 NCAA Division III National Championship by 42 points in Cedar Rapids, opens the 2026-27 season ranked first in the tournament team top 25 with 62 points.

title: With 86 straight dual wins, Penn State opens season ranked No. 1
body: Manheim, Pennsylvania – Returning national team champion Penn State, riding an NCAA record 86 match win streak, opens the season as the unanimous No. 1 in the NWCA Division I Men's Wrestling Coaches Poll presented by Theraworx.

title: Alvernia Names Arentz Next Women’s Wrestling Coach
body: Reading, Pa. (September 24, 2026) - Alvernia University's Director of Athletics and Recreation Cory Beddick announced the hiring of Kenny Arentz as the next Women's Wrestling coach on Thursday.

title: David Bossardet Named Head Wrestling Coach
body: (October 26, 2026) Mena, Arkansas – UA Rich Mountain & Bucks Athletics is excited to announce the addition of Men's & Women's Wrestling to begin in the 2027-2028 academic year with the hiring of David Bossardet as the Head Men's & Women's Wrestling Coach. Coach Bossardet comes to Mena via Florida, where he has been a teacher, wrestling coach, school administrator, and coordinator of safety for Flagler County Schools.

title: Women’s Wrestling: Mount Union Names Sugey Ceja New Head Coach
body: ALLIANCE, Ohio – The University of Mount Union has selected Sugey Ceja to lead its women's wrestling program, bringing an impressive resume as a national collegiate finalist and a successful NCAA coach.

title: Taygen Smith Named as Chadron State Men's Wrestling Coach
body: CHADRON, Neb. – Chadron State Athletics has announced the hiring of former CSC assistant Taygen Smith as the school's new head men's wrestling coach.

title: Trinity Wrestling Announces Coaching Transition
body: HARTFORD, Conn. – Trinity College has announced a transition in leadership of its wrestling program, as longtime head coach Sebastian "Sebby" Amato is retiring from coaching and Brendan Weirhas been named the Bantams' new head wrestling coach, effective September of 2026.

title: Mulder Tabbed as Pioneers Women's Wrestling Head Coach
body: PLATTEVILLE, Wis. – Emma Mulder has been named the first-ever head coach of the University of Wisconsin-Platteville women's wrestling team, announced Tuesday by Director of Athletics and Recreation Sam Koenig.

title: Vikings Emerge as Top Team in NAIA Women’s Wrestling Preseason Rating
body: KANSAS CITY, MO.- Grand View women's wrestling was tabbed No. 1 for the NAIA Women's Wrestling Preseason Rating after totaling 187 points. Indiana Tech trails in second with 159 points, and Ottawa (Kan.) sits in third with 152. Life (Ga.) and Wayland Baptist (Texas) are ranked fourth and fifth, respectively.
